why: Both app lanes consume the platform's UI packages from a local feed built out of a sibling
platform checkout. The feed directories are gitignored, so a clean CI runner had no package
source at all and every restore failed NU1301 - which is why this repository's only workflow
had been red on every run, main included, and why the React lane's tests had never executed
CI now checks the platform out at THIS commit and builds both feeds from it. Pinning rather
than tracking the platform's default branch is deliberate: a floating checkout would turn app
CI red for platform reasons unrelated to the app pull request under test, which is the failure
mode that trains people to ignore a red build.
Publishing the platform's UI packages to a registry and consuming them by version remains the
durable answer and would remove the feed mechanism from CI entirely. It needs a release cadence
the platform does not have yet, so this pin is the step that makes CI honest in the meantime.
producersWhy: Control ticket 105 acceptance 3. Two repositories declared eight identical PackageIds, and
three of the ids this lane consumes were among them. The feed directories are gitignored, so
nothing recorded WHICH repository packed the bytes the app shipped - only the disk it was
built on knew. The id cannot tell two producers apart; the assembly inside can.
harborline-api stopped producing these ids on 2026-08-24 (it now packs three Api.* packages
and nothing else), so there is exactly one producer today. This block is what makes that a
checked fact rather than a coincidence of the current trees.
Control ticket 063 wave 1 renamed the platform's project and assembly identities.
The failing producer check was observed while moving this pin,
then this block was updated from the assemblies emitted by the pinned feed build.
packageVersion: There is no package VERSION to pin. Platform ticket 143 derives every package version from a
hash of the platform's packable content, so a repack of a changed tree is a new version and a
cached extraction can never shadow it. apps/blazor/scripts/build-local-feed.mjs computes it by
importing the platform's own tooling/package-version.mjs out of this pinned checkout - the same
function the platform's consumer fixtures call - and writes it to apps/blazor/.feed/packed-version.props,
which the root Directory.Packages.props imports. Moving this commit is therefore the whole
re-pin: rebuild the feed and the version follows, with no version edited by hand anywhere.
bump: Move the commit when the app needs a platform change. Rebuild both feeds locally first
(npm run feed in apps/react, node scripts/build-local-feed.mjs in apps/blazor), run both
suites, and land the pin in the same change as whatever needed it - so the reason the pin
moved is legible in one diff.
